findings.title: Early interpolation defeats $__range split guard and freezes range
findings.body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target before querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable is checked. applyTemplateVariables expands template variables (new test proves it expands $__auto and $step), so it will also expand $__range/$__range_s/$__range_ms before the guard sees them. The guard !isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) will then pass and a query that must not be split will be split. All split sub-requests will carry $__range/$__interval frozen to the full-range value instead of per-split-range backend interpolation described in the code comment, returning wrong data.

findings.title: Double interpolation duplicates ad-hoc filters
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery interpolates with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery via subRequest={...request, targets:...} which interpolates again with the same scopedVars/filters. The updated test expecting 5 calls for 1 target confirms the double pass. Applying template variables with request.filters rewrites expr to add ad-hoc filters; running it twice appends them twice and re-expands variables, producing over-constrained/wrong LogQL and wasted work. Interpolation with filters should happen once.

findings.title: Empty check runs before interpolation
findings.body: runSplitQuery filters with .filter((query)=>query.expr) before .map((query)=>datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)). A query whose raw expr is truthy but interpolates to empty (e.g. expr is a variable that is empty/undefined) passes the filter and then flows into isLogsQuery/partition/grouping and datasource.runQuery. This issues backend requests for empty queries and can misclassify them. The same pattern exists in shardQuerySplitting.ts. Filter for empty expr after interpolation.
